title: Flat lower truncation and its bounded-above K-flat kernel
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring and $T$ a scheme. Work on a small skeleton of $T_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site; def-weil-size-convention] with constant ring sheaf $\Lambda_T$ [def-kun-constant-sheaf]. Let $K^\bullet$ be an integer-indexed cochain complex of $\Lambda_T$-module sheaves [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] with flat terms [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], and let $a\in\mathbf Z$. Assume $H^i(K^\bullet)=0$ for every $i<a$ [def-pc-acyclic-complex-modules] and assume that $N=\operatorname{coker}(d^{a-1}:K^{a-1}\to K^a)$ is flat. Put $P^\bullet=\tau_{\ge a}K^\bullet$ [def-kun-truncations], with terms $0$ for $i<a$, $N$ for $i=a$, and $K^i$ for $i>a$, and differential out of $N$ induced by $d^a$. Let $q:K^\bullet\to P^\bullet$ be zero below $a$, the cokernel projection at $a$, and the identity above $a$. Then $q$ is a quasi-isomorphism [def-pc-quasi-iso-modules] and $P^\bullet$ has flat terms. Its kernel $L^\bullet$ has terms $K^i$ for $i<a$, $I=\operatorname{im}(d^{a-1})$ for $i=a$, and $0$ for $i>a$, with the differential $K^{a-1}\to I$ the image factorization of $d^{a-1}$. The sheaf $I$ is flat, $L^\bullet$ is bounded above with flat terms and is K-flat [def-pc-kflat-complex], and $0\to L^\bullet\to K^\bullet\xrightarrow{q}P^\bullet\to0$ is short exact in every degree.

The component formulas pi_f_self and pi_f_above are proved from liftExtend and the restriction component formulas: at a the map is pOpcycles followed by the boundary isomorphism inverse, and above a it is the truncation identification inverse. proof.text: Apply CochainComplex.quasiIso_πTruncGE_iff. Its IsGE condition is equivalent to exactness in each degree i<a, which is equivalent to IsZero (K.homology i). This is exactly the vanishing hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 0F1M (lemma-bounded-below-tor-amplitude), proof: lower truncation and its kernel

proof.text: Evaluation preserves kernels, so evaluate the kernel fork of the quotient in each degree. Below a the quotient is zero and the kernel inclusion is invertible. Above a the quotient is invertible and its kernel is zero. At a cancel the invertible truncation identification to identify the evaluated kernel with a kernel of pOpcycles. The exact cokernel sequence of the incoming differential makes its categorical image another such kernel. Uniqueness of kernel limits supplies the boundary isomorphism commuting with inclusion. Cancel the image monomorphism in the chain-map identity for the kernel inclusion to obtain the asserted image-factorization differential. The quotient is epic in every degree; map its short exact kernel sequence through evaluation.

proof.text: Use the flat-quotient tensor-row argument of lem-weil-pbc-site-flat-quotient-tensor-ses, reusing its proved private mono_bottom_of_tensor_rows chase. Its public theorem identifies site and coefficient universes, so carry out its remaining formal argument in the general braided tensor category of module sheaves. Functorial flat covers are supplied by the proved independent-coefficient hasFunctorialFlatResolution_kfi API in lem-pc-kflat-resolution. Tensor preserves colimits by lem-weil-pbc-independent-sheaf-tensor-colimits. The siteSheafTensorRightIso comparison translates IsFlatOnSite to categorical tensor flatness and back. Apply the resulting kernel-flatness argument to image(d) -> K.X a -> K.opcycles a. Flatness is invariant under the displayed isomorphisms and holds for zero objects, proving termwise flatness of the truncation and kernel.

proof.text: The evaluated kernels vanish in every degree above a. Apply the first clause of etale_kflat_criteria to this upper bound and the proved flat terms. At this site the coefficient universe is the maximum of the site universes, so isKFlatIndependentCoefficients_iff_isKFlat identifies the conclusion directly with the required independent-coefficient predicate. No derived tensor or symmetry comparison is needed.
